description: Triage register for @trailofbits/vsix-audit findings on the roo-plus VSIX. Every entry is a finding that a maintainer has characterized as by-design (content coincidence, bundled OSS, data/prose/source-map/grammar/WASM bytes, or declared capability). scripts/vsix-audit.mjs fails closed on any finding NOT listed here, on any severity/count escalation above the recorded baseline, and on degraded coverage (YARA-X unavailable) in a publish context; the release-validation and publish workflows run it as an ADVISORY step (VSIX_AUDIT_ENFORCE=false). See SECURITY.md 'Optional on-demand VSIX audit' + DEBT #23.

stages: oversized-yara: pinned yr v1.20.0 + the tool's own zoo/signatures/yara/*.yar over every packaged file > 10 MiB

oversizedFiles.note: The ONLY packaged file above 10 MiB. Stage 1 never YARA-scans it (`dist/scanner/checks/yara.js` skips buffer.length > 10 MiB); stage 2 does, and all 19 matches are individually triaged in this revision.

scan.note: Full-coverage scan of the 3.89.1 artefact built from the current tree (1,286 files, 39.14 MB) with the pinned YARA-X v1.20.0 release asset (tarball sha256 cabb8df46492fff59c51261302c71ed9cb2cef393d3f0ca560801a34a8e24cbe verified before use). 187 findings across 21 files: 168 from stage 1 (all matched existing entries, including the 3.89.1 changelog.md and re-hashed mermaid triage) plus 19 from the new oversized-file stage on dist/extension.js. `coverage: full` for this entry means BOTH: stage 1 reported no degradation AND stage 2 had yr plus the rule set and scanned every oversized file. Supersedes the 3.87.3 baseline (d60a9adbeb3c107b6db3cea494c9a02cee45439766343f96d64392b5e424e514, 2026-09-08) and the 2026-10-21 stage-1-only scan (f22360f638f76aaafaadeae4fc925a4acc6883d84fd54bcb74c853a4695dedc6, 168 findings, 13 unregistered, coverage that did NOT include dist/extension.js).

remap.reason: Issue #13 webview chunk consolidation renamed the hashed webview chunks (and Sub-task B Curated Shiki removed the common-lisp grammar).
remap.method: DETERMINISTIC REMAP (no re-scan). The register tool resolves (@trailofbits/vsix-audit@0.3.0 via npx) but YARA-X is not installed, so a full-coverage scan cannot be reproduced; regenerating would have produced degraded coverage. Each entry keyed to a hashed webview chunk was re-pointed to the current build file carrying the same module identity, resolved from the production source maps. Where several old chunks collapsed into one new chunk, their counts were summed (the gate only fails when findings EXCEED the recorded count, so a summed cap is conservative).
remap.limitation: Filename-level remap only: rules/severities are carried over unchanged from the last full-coverage scan (3.87.3), so this is NOT a re-verified scan. A maintainer must regenerate with YARA-X present before relying on it as a fresh baseline. The scan.* block still describes the original 3.87.3 full-coverage scan.
remap.regeneration: MUST be regenerated with @trailofbits/vsix-audit (pinned 0.3.0) WITH YARA-X (v1.20.0) present before this register is treated as a fresh baseline; a YARA-X-less run is degraded coverage and must never be recorded as a baseline (scripts/vsix-audit.mjs fails closed on that in a publish context). The same run now also executes the oversized-file stage, so `yr` and the tool's rule set must be on the host or the coverage line reports the gap instead of saying `coverage: full`. REGISTER IDENTITY IS NORMALISED, NOT LITERAL: every entry still records the exact path that was triaged, but `classifyFindings` compares `normalizeFileKey(entry.file)` with `normalizeFileKey(finding.location.file)`, which replaces the TRAILING 1-2 content-hash segments of a `.js`/`.js.map` bundle with `-<hash>` (e.g. `mermaid~…~ganttDiagram-~gdd5p7yb-DHB4NmXe.js` -> `mermaid~…~ganttDiagram--<hash>.js`). A webview rebuild that re-hashes chunks therefore keeps matching its registered family instead of forcing a bulk re-accept; files with no hash suffix (`changelog.md`, `dist/extension.js`, `dist/workers/countTokens.js`, ...) are compared exactly, so exact matching remains the default. Within one family the caps combine strictly: the LOWEST registered severity and the LARGEST per-file count. A NEW family, a new rule inside a family, a raised severity or more hits than the baseline still fails the gate. The 2026-10-06 note that claimed this entry's `file` 'was corrected from `changelog.md` to the packaged `CHANGELOG.md` (the pack ships the uppercase name and the scanner preserves case)' was WRONG and is withdrawn: the packaged artefact ships the lowercase name and the entry is keyed to `changelog.md` as of the 2026-10-21 rescan (verification recorded in `rescan2026_10_21.pathCaseVerification`). See SECURITY.md 'Optional on-demand VSIX audit' + DEBT #23.

rescan2026_10_21.artefact: roo-plus-3.89.1.vsix (built from the current tree with `pnpm --filter ./src vsix`)
rescan2026_10_21.coverage: full — YARA-X v1.20.0 on PATH, pinned release asset extracted and its tarball sha256 verified against the workflows' pin; scanner metadata reported degraded:false with no warnings
rescan2026_10_21.findings: 168 total; 155 matched existing entries; 13 unregistered (1 CRITICAL, 12 MEDIUM)
rescan2026_10_21.changes: ADDED 12 individually justified entries for the re-hashed mermaid chunks (11 x YARA_SUSP_JS_Decimal_Byte_Array_Jan25, 1 x YARA_SUSP_JS_Hex_Escape_Chain_Jan25); CORRECTED the YARA_STEALER_JS_Credential_File_Exfil_Jan25 entry key from `CHANGELOG.md` to `changelog.md`. No rule class, severity cap or baseline count was widened.
rescan2026_10_21.pathCaseVerification: Determined from the artefact, not from the scan result: `unzip -l bin/roo-plus-3.89.1.vsix | grep -i changelog` lists `388018  extension/changelog.md` and `extension/CHANGELOG.md` does not exist (0 matches). @trailofbits/vsix-audit@0.3.0 reports that entry verbatim as `changelog.md`. There is no case-normalising or remapping step in scripts/vsix-audit.mjs — classifyFindings compares `entry.file` to `finding.location.file` with strict equality — so the recorded path was a factually wrong string, not a symptom of a remap bug. No remap logic was changed.
rescan2026_10_21.retained: Entries for chunk names the current build no longer emits (3.87.3-era hashed names and .js.map paths, and the withdrawn `CHANGELOG.md` key is gone) are retained as triage history; an entry that matches nothing neither widens nor narrows the gate.
rescan2026_10_21.rebuildStability: Two consecutive `pnpm --filter ./src vsix` builds from the identical tree produced byte-DIFFERENT archives with IDENTICAL payloads: sha256 29c84ead492db1c27937d35e45e3b0009821945ee9e8d72a43eb49058d041b0a (build 1) and 3ef9fc5deeb4ad7e9bb62ecfacb05f9d7fc44218e71da80c90b88df437476a28 (build 2), both 1,286 entries / 115,160,730 uncompressed bytes with every entry CRC-32 and size identical; the only differing bytes are the DOS modification-time fields vsce stamps into each ZIP header (observed at offset 10-13 of the first local header). vsce packaging is therefore not byte-reproducible, so the gate is proven stable on CONTENT rather than on archive bytes. A THIRD artefact - the pre-existing bin/roo-plus-3.89.1.vsix from the same tree (f22360f638f76aaafaadeae4fc925a4acc6883d84fd54bcb74c853a4695dedc6) built with a differently-hashed webview output - also passes: its 12 re-hashed mermaid chunks and 2 re-named chunk families match their registered families through normalizeFileKey instead of turning the gate red. All three ran with exit 0, coverage: full, 187 findings, 187 by-design.
rescan2026_10_21.coverageLimitation: RESOLVED (2026-10-21, second pass). Recorded originally as: @trailofbits/vsix-audit@0.3.0 skips files larger than 10 MiB for the YARA stage (`dist/scanner/checks/yara.js`: `if (buffer.length > 10 * 1024 * 1024) continue;`), so the 15,059,325-byte `dist/extension.js` received AST/other checks but no YARA rule evaluation, and `coverage: full` attested only that YARA-X was available. The wrapper now runs its own second stage (`runOversizedStage`): it enumerates every packaged file above the same 10 MiB threshold from the VSIX central directory, scans each with the pinned `yr` binary and the tool's own rule set, and maps matches into the tool's finding shape. All 19 matches on dist/extension.js (not 3 - a full `yr scan --print-strings` of the bundle matches 19 rules) are triaged above with quoted bytes and offsets. `coverage: full` now means stage 1 clean AND YARA-X present AND every oversized file scanned.
